intro: Booking, ordering, asking for things during the meal, mentioning a problem and paying: in a restaurant, everything is said with a few polite phrases. This lesson builds on “would like” (lesson 34) and adds the customs of English-speaking countries (tips, cooking a steak, allergies).
objectifs: Book a table on the phone and say who you are when you arrive.
Order a full meal politely (I'll have…, Could I have…?) and mention how you want food cooked or an allergy.
Ask for things during the meal and mention a problem without being rude.
Ask for the bill, pay and understand tipping customs.

texte: To book: “I'd like to book a table for four for Saturday at eight, please.” The restaurant asks: “What name is it, please?” / “Can I have a name for the booking?” Answer: “It's under the name Diallo.”
When you arrive: “Hello, we have a reservation for eight o'clock. The name's Diallo.” or, with no booking: “Have you got a table for two?” / “A table for two, please.”
Careful: don't say “We are four”. Say “There are four of us” or simply “A table for four, please”.
exemples: I'd like to book a table for six on Friday evening.
Good evening. Have you got a table for three? — Inside or on the terrace?
There are five of us. Can we sit by the window?

texte: The waiter asks: “Are you ready to order?”, “What would you like to drink?”, “What can I get you?”. If you are not ready: “Could we have a few more minutes, please?”
To order, the natural phrases are “I'll have…”, “Could I have…?” and “I'd like…”. Avoid “I take…” and “I want…”.

The meal: “a starter” (UK; US “appetizer”) = the first, small dish; “a main course” (US “entrée”!) = the main dish; “a dessert”; “a side dish” = extra food with the main dish; “the dish of the day” = the special dish today.

lignes: Yes. For my starter, I'll have the soup.
Could I have the grilled chicken, please?
How would you like your steak?
Medium, please. (rare = red inside, medium = pink inside, well done = cooked all through)
Would you like any side dishes?
Yes, some chips and a salad.
A bottle of still water, please. (still = without bubbles, sparkling = with bubbles)
No, thank you. Just a coffee.

exemples: What do you recommend? — The fish is excellent today.
I'm allergic to nuts. Is there any peanut in this sauce?
I'm vegetarian. Have you got any dishes without meat?

texte: To call the waiter politely: “Excuse me!” with a small hand sign (never click your fingers). To ask for things: “Could we have some more bread, please?”, “Could I have another glass of water?”, “Could you bring me a spoon?”
The waiter may say: “Enjoy your meal!” and come back to ask: “Is everything OK?” / “How is everything?” Answer: “It's delicious, thank you.”
To mention a problem politely: “Excuse me, I think there's a mistake. I ordered the fish, not the chicken.”, “I'm sorry, but my soup is cold.”
exemples: Excuse me, could we have some more napkins, please?
How is everything? — Lovely, thanks. The sauce is delicious.
Sorry, but this isn't what I ordered. I asked for the vegetarian pasta.
sections.note: On the table: a knife, a fork, a spoon, a teaspoon, a napkin (UK also serviette), a plate, a glass.

texte: For the bill: “Could we have the bill, please?” (UK) / “Could we have the check, please?” (US). Useful questions: “Can we pay separately?”, “Can I pay by card?”, “Is service included?”.

Tipping (“a tip”) is different in each country: in the UK, about 10 to 12.5% if service is not included; in the USA and Canada, people leave 15 to 20% (it is almost expected); in France, Belgium and Cameroon, it is optional.
“Keep the change” is an easy way to leave a tip in cash.
exemples: Could we have the bill, please? — Of course. Together or separately?
Is service included? — No, it isn't.

formule: I'd like to book a table for… · A table for two, please. · I'll have… / Could I have…? · Could we have the bill, please?
prononciation: “I'll have” is /aɪl hæv/; in fast speech the h is often weak: “I'll 'ave the fish”.
“dessert” /dɪˈzɜːt/ (stress at the end, with /z/) ≠ “desert” /ˈdezət/ (a dry, sandy place).
“Could we have…”: /kʊd wi hæv/; let your voice go up a little at the end to sound polite: “…the BILL, please? ↗”.
erreurs: I'll have the chicken. / Could I have the chicken?
To order: I'll have / Could I have.
The bill, please. (US: The check, please.)
There are four of us. / A table for four, please.
I'd like my steak rare, please.
For entrée, I'll have the soup. (UK)
For my starter, I'll have the soup.
In the UK the first dish is a starter; in the US “entrée” is the main course.

dialogue.contexte: In a restaurant in Brussels, Grace (from Nairobi) and her colleague Thomas have a business lunch.
lignes: Good afternoon. Are you ready to order?
The dish of the day is mussels with chips. It's very popular.
Perfect, I'll have the mussels, please.
I'm allergic to shellfish. Could I have the vegetable lasagne?
A bottle of sparkling water, please.
Here you are. Enjoy your meal!
Excuse me, could we have the bill, please? Can I pay by card?
Yes, of course. Service is included.
No need for a big tip.

mots: I'd like to book a table.
ask for a table or room for a later time
We have a reservation for eight.
a table or room that is kept for you
For my main course, I'll have the fish.
the biggest dish of a meal (US: entrée)
Rice comes as a side dish.
extra food served with the main dish
cooked only a little, red inside
My son is allergic to eggs.
becoming ill when you eat or touch something
Could we have the bill, please?
a paper that shows how much to pay (US: check)

exercices.consigne: Who says this: the waiter or the customer?
items: How would you like your steak?
Could we have the bill, please?
I'd like to ___ a table for two.
For my ___, I'll have the soup. (the first dish, UK)

exercices.consigne: Make the sentence polite and natural.
items: Could I have the menu, please?
Could we have some more bread, please?
Could we have the bill, please?
A table for three, please. / There are three of us.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: I take the dish of the day.
I'll have the dish of the day.
I'd like my steak at point.
I'd like my steak medium, please.
Excuse me, this isn't what I commanded.
Excuse me, this isn't what I ordered.

exercices.consigne: Write an eight-line dialogue in a restaurant: arriving, ordering (starter, main course, drink), a small problem, the bill.
items: Waiter: Good evening. Have you got a reservation? Me: Yes, it's under the name Mbarga, for two. Waiter: This way, please. Are you ready to order? Me: Yes. For my starter, I'll have the avocado salad, and then the grilled fish with plantain. Waiter: And to drink? Me: A bottle of still water, please. … Excuse me, I think there's a mistake: I ordered plantain, not rice. Waiter: I'm so sorry, I'll change it. Me: Thank you. Could we have the bill, please?

a_retenir: Book: I'd like to book a table for four at eight. Arrive: A table for two, please. / We have a reservation.
Order: I'll have… / Could I have…?; starter (UK) = first dish, main course (US entrée!).
Be exact: rare / medium / well done; I'm allergic to…; I'm vegetarian.
During the meal: Excuse me, could we have…?; Enjoy your meal!; complain politely: I'm sorry, but…
Pay: Could we have the bill (US check), please? Is service included? Tip 15–20% in the USA and Canada.
